title: Am I Audio launches I Am Choir, an AI vocal plug-in built with credited, royalty-sharing singers
excerpt: Am I Audio has launched I Am Choir, an AI vocal plug-in that turns a single vocal take into a full choral arrangement. It was built with singers who were credited, compensated and share in royalties — a consent-first model for AI vocal tooling.
rationale: A shipping plug-in that changes a session tomorrow — one take becomes a choir — and it pairs the capability with a credited, royalty-sharing consent model that sets a bar for AI vocal tools.

title: Push Hack opens Ableton Push 3's display, files and MIDI — built with AI coding agents
excerpt: Federico Pepe's Push Hack opens up Ableton Push 3's display, file system, MIDI and LEDs via SSH — and he built it with AI-assisted coding agents, arguing reverse-engineering is exactly what ML is good at. A concrete look at AI agents as instrument-modding tools.
rationale: The most actionable new use of AI in the pool: coding agents used to reverse-engineer closed hardware, turning a Push 3 into an open, hackable instrument surface.

title: Spotify adds Merlin to its AI music remix and covers effort
excerpt: Merlin, representing 30,000+ independent labels, joins Universal in backing Spotify's AI-powered remix and covers product. The paid tool will let fans generate AI covers and remixes of opted-in artists, with credit and compensation attached.
rationale: With Merlin's 30,000+ indie labels on board, Spotify's fan-facing AI remix tool moves from rumour to imminent — the biggest distribution shift in the pool. Chosen over the MBW and Billboard versions of the same story.

title: Suno Vinyl presses your AI-generated tracks onto custom 12-inch records
excerpt: Suno has announced Suno Vinyl, a service that presses tracks from a user's AI-generated library onto custom 12-inch records with designed sleeves, around $45 per record. Prompt-made music gets a physical, art-directed output format.
rationale: Novel and design-relevant: prompt-generated audio gets an art-directed physical object, pulling sleeve design and packaging into the generative-music workflow.

title: Key EU AI Act rules are now being enforced — what that means for music
excerpt: The EU AI Act's transparency rules came into force on 2 August, and Music Ally breaks down what they mean in practice — most immediately for the AI tools musicians already use, including labelling of AI-generated output.
rationale: Rules that are live, not proposed: transparency and labelling obligations that reach the AI tools producers already have open, so it changes what they must disclose today.
